title: What do the numbers in the count of two end in?
description: Counting in twos builds a strip of numbers, and the video reads the last digit of each one. The pattern settles six hundred and eighty two and eight thousand five hundred and sixty, and Keeko's doubt, that a zero at the end is not even, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: the last digit of a number in the count of two is zero, two, four, six or eight, in turn. Watch for students who think a zero at the end does not count as an even digit.

source: What is the pattern in the last digit of the multiples of 2? Is 682 divisible by 2? Is 8560?
video_script.why: The child sees the pattern in the last digit of the count of two and uses it to test six hundred and eighty two and eight thousand five hundred and sixty.
video_script.substitution: Count in twos, read the last digits, and test any number by its last digit.
video_script.anchor: a strip of number cards counting in twos from 2, with the last digit of each card lit
video_script.wrong_answer: a number that ends in zero is not divisible by two
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says a number that ends in zero is not divisible by two, because zero is not even. Ten and twenty are in the count of two and end in zero, so the bubble is struck through.
video_script.payoff_line: Both numbers are divisible by two

final_answer.value: Last digit 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8; both 682 and 8560 are divisible by 2
final_answer.spoken: the last digit is zero, two, four, six or eight, and both six hundred and eighty two and eight thousand five hundred and sixty are divisible by two

hold_back: Answer: Last digit 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8; both 682 and 8560 are divisible by 2
maths_rules: the last digits go 2, 4, 6, 8, 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 0, so the last digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8
0 = 2 x 0, so zero is an even digit
video_script.design: One idea: the last digit of a multiple of two is zero, two, four, six or eight. Assumes skip counting. Wrong idea: a zero at the end is not even. The strip stays on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about counting in twos.
<bookmark mark='count'/>The count goes two, four, six, eight, ten, twelve.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What do the last digits show?
<bookmark mark='big'/>Does two divide six hundred and eighty two, and eight thousand five hundred and sixty?

beats.on_screen: the strip and the numbers hold still and the question stays on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: jumps of 2 from zero land on the cards one by one; the label multiple of 2

marks.jump: jumps of two from zero land on the cards one by one
marks.name: the label multiple of 2 is written over the cards

narration: <bookmark mark='jump'/>Start at zero and jump in twos.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Every number you land on is called a multiple of two.

The numbers are six hundred and eighty two, and eight thousand five hundred and sixty.

beats.on_screen: To find: the pattern in the last digit; is 682 divisible by 2; is 8560 divisible by 2

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find three things.
First, the pattern in the last digit.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Second and third, whether two divides each big number.

marks.count: the last digit of each card is lit in turn
marks.pat: the digits 2, 4, 6, 8 and 0 are shown going round again and again

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step one, read the last digit of each number in the count.
<bookmark mark='pat'/>It goes two, four, six, eight, zero, and then it goes round again.
The last digit is always zero, two, four, six or eight.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, 682 ends in 2, an even digit: 2 x 341 = 682

marks.last: the last digit 2 of 682 lights up
marks.tick: 2 x 341 = 682 is written and a tick appears

narration: <bookmark mark='last'/>Step two, read the last digit of six hundred and eighty two. It is two.
<bookmark mark='tick'/>Two times three hundred and forty one is six hundred and eighty two, so two divides it.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, 8560 ends in 0, an even digit: 2 x 4280 = 8560

marks.last: the last digit 0 of 8560 lights up
marks.tick: 2 x 4280 = 8560 is written and a tick appears

narration: <bookmark mark='last'/>Step three, read the last digit of the big number. It is zero.
<bookmark mark='tick'/>Two times four thousand two hundred and eighty is eight thousand five hundred and sixty. Two divides it too.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Last digit 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8; both 682 and 8560 are divisible by 2
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The last digit is zero, two, four, six or eight.
Both numbers are divisible by two.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the boxed answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble; the cards 10 and 20 on the strip light up with their zeros and the bubble is struck through

marks.doubt: the bubble appears over the number 8560
marks.zero: the cards 10 and 20 light up with their zeros

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks a number that ends in zero is not divisible by two, because zero is not even.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>But ten and twenty are in the count of two, and they end in zero.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Zero is one of the five endings of the count, and the count starts from it.
